title: Response-Specific Thermal Equivalence of Full-Scale Multi-Material Fire-Door Systems Under Seven Fire Histories
content: Fire-resistance classification relies on reproducible standard heating, whereas real and design fires can impose substantially different thermal histories. This study proposes a validity-aware procedure for assessing response-specific thermal equivalence in full-scale fire-door systems. Seven furnace histories were examined using wooden, glazed aluminium, and steel doors tested simultaneously within the same supporting construction. Thermal responses at the frame rebate, 25 mm and 100 mm from the visible leaf edge, and general leaf surface were compared at matched instantaneous furnace temperature and matched furnace-temperature area under the curve (AUC), using only valid pre-integrity-loss data. Because each fire history was represented by one furnace run, the analysis is descriptive rather than inferential. At 700 °C, frame-rebate temperature-rise spreads reached approximately 82–156 °C across technologies. Matching AUC = 5000 °C·min produced substantially closer agreement in leaf-related responses while large rebate differences remained. A fixed common-subset analysis using the same four fire histories for all technologies and AUC levels confirmed this response-location dependence in 54 of 54 comparisons. Furnace burner input did not define transferable severity or integrity thresholds. Thermal equivalence was therefore response- and technology-specific rather than a system-wide property.
